hardware: Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 (Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, 128 GiB unified, Desktop)
question: Does the Muse DFlash tuning (LDS-padded prefill/verify, adaptive-split shared decode attention, combine live-scan, norm) generalize to the real hipengine server API, or is it overfitted to the mtpbench harness?
server_command: hipengine serve --model Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf --speculative-provider dflash --draft-model dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf --kv-storage bf16 --max-context-tokens 8192 (under rocprofv3 --kernel-trace)
request_surface: OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions; DFlash selected per request with speculative:true (generic provider, explicit-only, raw-greedy BF16 c=1 guard); AR baseline omits speculative.
verdict: NOT overfitted. The tuned DFlash path runs through the real server API and is output-invariant: AR and DFlash return identical token IDs for short, completion, and 6011-token long-context prompts; repeat requests deterministic; buffered==streaming.

route_telemetry.note: hipengine.speculative_mtp extension reads used:false/draft_tokens:0 because that accounting is native-MTP-only and does not cover the generic provider; generation_shape.route='speculative' plus the DFlash-specific draft-kernel dispatches are the conclusive route evidence.

kernel_trace.interpretation: muse_glimmer_draft_flash_wmma_kernel (675) is DFlash-draft-specific and never runs in AR decode; its presence plus route='speculative' proves the tuned path executed, not an AR fallback. Seven distinct shared-decode grid.x configs (512..10240) show the adaptive split-block logic engaged across context lengths, including the 6011-token prompt past the 2048 crossing.

caveats: Correctness/path-engagement validation, not a server throughput claim; rocprofv3 trace adds overhead and no tok/s is asserted here. Performance claims remain with the mtpbench artifacts.

Muse DFlash on the server is explicit-only per request (speculative:true) and requires --speculative-provider dflash --draft-model <sidecar>; ordinary chat requests default to AR by documented design. --speculative-mtp-serving is the native-MTP flag and does not route Muse (run 1 used it by mistake and correctly fell back to AR).
